Thanks Elena — good set of questions. Short answers up front, details below:

1) BGP auth keys: Preferred pattern is customer-managed (best security/segregation) with Redwood operating a read-only copy for emergency failover. We can support customer KMS-backed storage; rotation is coordinated via playbook.
2) Circuit ownership: For lowest RTO we recommend a dual-terminated design where carrier handoff is on AvaTech side and Redwood terminates into a dedicated VPC/VLAN on our appliance. That lets us take over session state during warm failover without physical carrier swaps.
3) KMS residency: Yes — customer-managed keys (EU KMS) remain in-region. Metadata that must be replicated (eg. routing tags, state hashes) is stored encrypted using a region-scoped CMK; Redwood enforces strict IAM that disallows key export.

Action items I'm proposing:
- Marissa: produce a procurement annex and a carve-out clause for circuit custody during cutover (will attach a draft).
- Karthik & Soojin: review the diagram and mark required firewall/VLAN rules and peering ASNs.
- Elena: confirm whether AvaTech wants Redwood to terminate cross-connects or prefers a transit VLAN managed by AvaTech.

Note: I'll schedule a short tabletop for Wednesday to run through the playbook and BGP failover steps (30m).
